info.name: CodingAssist (Charge-Capture Pipeline)
info.description: Endpoints for the CodingAssist auto-coding & charge-capture pipeline: clinical documentation in, a compliance-enforced structured charge ticket out. Mirrors RadiologyReporter's text-pipeline architecture; the upstream_entities field lets this chain directly off RadiologyReporter's /api/v1/reports/generate output. See the sibling RAdiology project for that collection.

request.description: Reports service status, model configuration, and RAG readiness.
Returns counts and contents of the loaded NCCI PTP edits and MUE limits. No AI call.

item.name: Generate Charge (clean office visit, control case)

request.description: Baseline happy path: single document, no bundling conflicts, no necessity issues. Should code cleanly with zero compliance flags. Use this as the control case when validating that new rules don't false-positive on clean documentation.

item.name: Generate Charge (NCCI bundling: laparoscopy converted to open)

request.description: Documents a diagnostic laparoscopy converted to an open procedure in the same session. The diagnostic scope is NCCI-bundled into the definitive open procedure and is not separately billable. Tests whether the deterministic edit check catches the bundle instead of drafting both as separate charge lines.

Same joint-injection code documented six times for the same joint in one visit, exceeding the realistic Medically Unlikely Edit ceiling for that code. Tests whether the rules engine caps/flags units instead of drafting a 6-unit charge line.

Heavily negated note where the working diagnosis was ruled out by imaging. Coding the suspected condition as confirmed (e.g. K35.80 appendicitis) instead of the symptom code (R10.9) would be a compliance error. Also includes a procedure-adjacent finding with unspecified laterality to test modifier (50/RT/LT) handling when the source text is ambiguous.

item.name: Generate Charge (medical necessity gap: lumbar MRI)

request.description: MRI lumbar spine ordered for uncomplicated low back pain under 6 weeks duration, no red flags, no prior conservative therapy. Fails most LCD medical-necessity criteria for advanced imaging. Tests whether the necessity check flags a likely denial before the claim drafts, rather than silently coding the study as billable.

Two documents for the same encounter disagree on severity (non-perforated vs. perforated appendicitis). The correct ICD-10/CPT pair depends on the pathology report, not the surgeon's intra-op impression. Tests whether extraction reconciles across documents and prefers the more definitive source instead of taking the first one seen.

Clinical note text contains an embedded instruction-override attempt aimed at the LLM normalize/extract/draft phases. Tests that the pipeline treats document text strictly as data, never as instructions, and that injected text cannot upcode the visit, fabricate a diagnosis, or suppress compliance/necessity flags.

High-volume polytrauma encounter spanning five documents from different services, heavy on shorthand, with the same procedures (chest tube, central line) mentioned redundantly across documents. Stresses extraction throughput across many documents and cross-document deduplication -- a chest tube placed once in the ED note must not be billed three times because three later notes also mention it.

Simulates chaining off RadiologyReporter's existing /api/v1/reports/generate output (same patient_id and findings as RAdiology/tests/sample_xr_chest_003.json in the sibling repo): structured_entities from a prior radiology pipeline run are passed directly as upstream_entities, with documents reduced to just the indication line. Tests the bypass path that should ground straight to CPT/ICD-10 instead of re-running normalize/extract on text that was already structured.

request.description: Malformed administrative envelope: place_of_service is not a valid CMS POS code, rendering_provider_npi is the wrong length, payer_id is empty, and date_of_service is implausibly far in the future. Should be rejected at the validation layer (422) before any LLM call is made.
